title: Counselling vs Therapy vs Coaching: What's the Difference?
excerpt: A clear, jargon-free guide to how counselling, psychotherapy, and coaching differ — and how to choose what fits.

value.text: If you have ever tried to find support for a hard patch in your life, you will know how confusing the words can be. Counselling, psychotherapy, coaching — they sound similar, they overlap in places, and the people offering them do not always explain how they differ. This guide is here to make that clearer, in plain language, so you can choose what actually fits your situation.

The short version: these are related but distinct kinds of support, offered by different professionals for different purposes. Knowing what each one is for can save you a lot of time, and help you feel confident that you are asking for the right thing.

Counselling is a structured, confidential space to reflect on what is going on in your life and how you are relating to it. It works well with the ordinary but demanding stuff of being human: stress, overwhelm, exhaustion, a sense of feeling stuck, disconnection from yourself or the people around you, and the unsteadiness that comes with big life changes. The focus is on the present and the near future — making sense of where you are, and finding gentler, more sustainable ways forward.

As a Systemic and Integrative Counsellor, this is the support I offer. Systemic means I pay attention to the relationships and contexts you live within, not just what happens inside you. Integrative means I draw on more than one approach — including body-oriented work such as Somatic Experiencing — depending on what is useful for you. You can read more about how I think and work on my [about page](/about), and about the shape of the sessions themselves on the [work together page](/work-with-me).
What psychotherapy is — and where it differs

Psychotherapy is a separate, regulated field. In many countries it is a protected, medical or clinical service, provided by licensed psychotherapists, clinical psychologists, or psychiatrists. It typically involves the assessment and treatment of diagnosed mental health conditions, often over a longer period and at greater depth, and it may sit alongside medical care.

This is an important line, and I want to be clear about it: I do not provide psychotherapy, treatment, or diagnosis. Those belong to a different, regulated profession. Counselling and psychotherapy share some tools and a caring, attentive stance, but they are not the same service — and where a clinical condition needs assessment or treatment, that is work for a licensed psychotherapist or doctor, not a counsellor.

None of this is a ranking. One is not "deeper" or "better" than the other; they simply do different jobs. Many people move between them over a lifetime, and a good counsellor will always tell you honestly when what you need sits outside the scope of counselling.

Coaching is another distinct service, usually provided by coaches, and it tends to be goal- and performance-oriented. Think career direction, leadership, productivity, a specific project or transition you want to move through. Coaching generally looks forward — clarifying goals and building strategies to reach them — and is less concerned with the emotional history behind where you are.

There is genuine overlap with counselling, especially around life direction and change. The difference is one of emphasis. Coaching asks "where do you want to get to, and how?" Counselling makes more room for "how are you, really, and what is this experience asking of you?" — including the feelings, patterns, and pressures underneath the goals.
You do not need a perfect diagnosis of your own situation before you reach out. But a few gentle questions can point you in the right direction:

items: If you are living with a diagnosed mental health condition, or you feel you may need clinical assessment or treatment, psychotherapy or medical care is the right place to start.
If you are carrying stress, overwhelm, exhaustion, or a sense of being stuck, and you want a reflective space to understand it and find your footing, counselling is likely a good fit.
If you have a clear external goal and want structured support to reach it, coaching may serve you best.
If you are simply not sure, it is completely fine to say so — a short conversation usually makes the picture much clearer.

value.text: This is exactly what a first, no-pressure conversation is for. If you would like help working out whether counselling fits what you are going through, you are welcome to [book a discovery call](/contact) or look through the [frequently asked questions](/faq) first. And if it turns out that what you need lies elsewhere, I will say so plainly and point you in a more helpful direction.
The most important thing is not getting the label exactly right on the first try. It is taking the step of asking for support — and trusting that the right kind of help can be found.
